english.title: Fail to deliver declaration under s. 89 to registrar within prescribed time
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were

(A)_[a company which]_
(B)_[an officer of a company, namely **(..SPECIFY COMPANY..), who]_

was in default in that a statutory declaration of solvency required by section 89(3) of the Insolvency Act 1986 was not delivered to the registrar of companies before the expiration of 15 days immediately following the date on which the resolution for the voluntary winding up of the company was passed
english.legislation: Contrary to section 89(6) and Schedule 10 of the Insolvency Act 1986.

english.notes:
(i) Ifa declaration required by section 89(3) to be delivered to the registrar is notso delivered within the time prescribed by that subsection, the company andevery officer in default is guilty of an offence.
(ii) Section 431 of the Insolvency Act 1986 providesthat notwithstanding anything in section 127(1) of the Magistrates' Courts Act1980, an information relating to such an offence which is triable by amagistrates' court in England and Wales may be so tried if it is laid at anytime within 3 years after the commission of the offence and within 12 monthsafter the date on which evidence sufficient in the opinion of the Director ofPublic Prosecutions or the Secretary of State (as the case may be) to justifythe proceedings comes to his knowledge. Summary proceedings in Scotland forsuch an offence shall not be commenced after the expiration of 3 years from thecommission of the offence.
